title: Life Reflect – Life review, meaningfulness, and emotional processing among patients in palliative care units
summary:
Life reflection at the end of life is a central theme in palliative medicine. Studies show that existential questions—such as regret, unfulfilled life goals, but also spiritual gratitude—become massively important in the final phase of life (Chochinov et al., 2005; Breitbart et al., 2015). Life review interventions and dignity therapy have a proven positive effect on emotional stability, grief processing, and sense of meaning in the care of the dying.
Despite the established palliative care system, there is a lack of systematic data on the importance of biographical review, conscious engagement with the current illness, and subjective feelings of regret or satisfaction when looking back on one's own life.
conditions: Patients undergoing treatment in a palliative care unit

interventions.name: Mixed-methods study with detailed qualitative interviews and a standardized questionnaire survey in the palliative care unit of the Medical University of Lausitz – Carl Thiem.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years
Diagnosed advanced tumor disease with palliative objectives
Cognitive ability to participate (Mini-Cog test ≥ 3)
Capacity to give consent
Exclusion criteria:
Acute confusion or delirium
Language barrier
Severe depressive episode
Missing consent
